scope: The MP003 method summary, dosing-design table and parameter boundaries presented immediately before approval. The saved profile expresses these decisions in the existing library schema. Method planning only; numerical execution and dataset qualification remain downstream.
approved_rule_text: Propose NCA methods for CL and Vss separately according to dosing design and parameter definition. Distinguish absolute from apparent parameters and require the appropriate exposure, moment and input-duration information. Reviewed NCA estimates may enter extrapolation review without a compartmental fit, while unsupported parameters remain explicit gaps.

approved_profile.name: NCA clearance and steady-state distribution volume
outputs: CL/F when absolute clearance is not identified
approved_profile.applies_when: The objective needs animal disposition parameters, including parameters intended for later extrapolation. Inherit MP001 and applicable MP002 requirements. This step proposes methods and identifies missing inputs; numerical estimation and qualification of the resulting parameters remain downstream.
required_inputs: Route, administered dose, analyte, concentration basis and parameter units, including whether quantities are absolute or body-weight-normalized.
Exposure and, for Vss, moment/residence-time information appropriate to the dosing design.
Dosing design and, for IV infusion, input-duration information needed by the proposed method.
conditional_inputs: Confirmed steady state, dosing interval and matching interval exposure when proposing steady-state clearance estimation.
A justified independent bioavailability estimate applicable to the study if converting CL/F to CL.
acceptable_alternatives: Reviewed NCA estimates may enter extrapolation review without a compartmental fit; qualify each parameter separately.
Report CL/F under its actual definition when an extravascular study does not identify absolute clearance.
preflight_checks: Propose NCA methods for CL and Vss separately according to dosing design and parameter definition. Distinguish absolute from apparent parameters and require the appropriate exposure, moment and input-duration information.
For single-dose IV clearance, propose Dose/AUCinf when the method assumptions apply. Do not substitute AUC0-24 for AUCinf merely because the finite window is available.
For verified steady-state interval methods, match dose and AUC to the same dosing interval and retain the route-specific distinction between CL and CL/F.

For IV Vss, propose CL multiplied by the appropriate MRT, with the AUC/AUMC and infusion-input treatment specified. Suitable single-dose IV data may support Vss; its name does not require steady-state repeat dosing.
Distinguish Vss from Vz, Vc and apparent volumes. Knowing F alone does not justify using an oral MRT directly as the disposition MRT for Vss.
Preserve plasma versus blood, total versus free, and L/h versus L/h/kg or corresponding volume definitions; do not combine incompatible parameter definitions.
post_analysis_checks: Downstream: review the supporting exposure and moment calculations, input-duration treatment, assumptions and available uncertainty separately for CL and Vss.

Downstream: submit each qualified parameter with its method, definitions, limitations and unresolved gaps for extrapolation review. Do not count a species for a parameter before that parameter is qualified.
approved_profile.missing_effect: Keep unsupported parameters and their missing prerequisites explicit. A supported CL does not automatically establish Vss. Retain independently supported results without silently changing the proposal's requested exposure window or parameter definition.
not_established: A compartmental curve shape from NCA CL and Vss alone.
Absolute clearance merely from an extravascular dose when F is unknown.
Interchangeability of Vss, Vz, Vc or apparent volumes.
Validity of every NCA parameter solely because another parameter is supported.

verification_scope: Existing library schema and approval-record binding only; no numerical analysis or empirical method test.
